title: Nepal tragedy: Owners missing, dog refuses to leave flood-hit Trishuli home
content: A black-and-white dog remains at the site of four homes destroyed by a flood.  He refuses to leave the muddy patch where his home once stood.  Rescue workers and JCBs clear debris around the steadfast canine.  Volunteers offer food and water, which he accepts quietly when alone.  Displaced residents understand his loyalty to his former territory.

title: No roofs, no toilets, no teachers: TOI check finds minuses in Rajasthan govt schools
content: TOI reporters visited govt schools in 6 Rajasthan districts after the CJP row. The findings show how basic govt schooling has collapsed in pockets of the state, from the coaching capital of Kota to desert villages and Jhalawar’s tragedy-hit Piplodi.

title: Haldwani ‘purification’ row: Day after FIR against Rahul, BJP, Cong trade barbs
content: The Congress party slammed the FIR against Rahul Gandhi, calling it casteist.  BJP countered that Rahul raised the issue belatedly after a threat from Kharge.  An FIR was registered against Rahul Gandhi under various sections and the SC/ST Act.  The complainant alleged Rahul gave a caste angle to cleaning work at the rally.  Uttarakhand CM stated state residents are unaware of Kharge's caste.

title: Major shake-up in Pakistan cricket: Seven players, coaches Sarfaraz, Gul released
content: Following a string of losses, the Pakistan Cricket Board has made significant changes by releasing seven players and parts of the coaching staff. Five new uncapped players have been brought on board, while Sarfaraz Ahmed and Umar Gul step aside from their coaching positions. Mike Hesson and Ashley Noffke will now oversee the coaching duties as the team readies itself for the third Test match against England at Edgbaston.

title: Government terms arbitration award on Indus Waters Treaty ‘illegal’
content: In a decisive move, India has dismissed an arbitration court's ruling related to the Indus Waters Treaty, asserting that the court lacks authority over sovereign matters. This echoes India's previous stance on a similar arbitration award. The Permanent Court of Arbitration urged India to respect its treaty obligations, but India firmly reaffirms that its suspension of treaty enforcement remains effective.

title: Oracle layoffs: Company leadership may again send the '6 am' email on September 1
content: Oracle employees expect layoff emails on September 1, the day its fiscal second quarter begins, with managers asked to submit lists of affected employees and some teams facing double-digit cuts. Staff fear a repeat of March 31, when a 6 am email from "Oracle Leadership" told 10,000 workers their role was eliminated. Oracle has already cut 21,000 jobs this fiscal year while spending $55.7 billion on AI data centres.

title: It's time to move from endless war to end of war: PM Modi to Putin
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged President Vladimir Putin to end the ongoing conflict. He emphasized that humanity's well-being depends on moving from endless war to peace. India supports all efforts to resolve issues peacefully and swiftly. Discussions also covered expanding cooperation in various key sectors. Both leaders agreed to maintain contact to strengthen their partnership.

title: Iran president meets PM Modi, seeks help to end war
content: Prime Minister Modi convened with Iranian President Pezeshkian to advance discussions on fortifying trade connections between their nations. Both leaders acknowledged the critical role of maritime freedom and trade in the region. They also discussed the ongoing situations in West Asia, focusing on the importance of Chabahar port collaboration. President Pezeshkian encouraged India to mediate for peace, underscoring their shared dedication to enhancing bilateral economic cooperation.

title: OpenClaw that Sam Altman spent billions on gets 'largest update in its history'
content: OpenClaw has unveiled its most comprehensive software upgrade yet with the arrival of version 2.0. This update enhances user accessibility significantly and integrates features for multi-user collaboration. Installation has been streamlined, along with expanded cross-platform automation tools. The redesigned browser interface provides a centralized workspace that improves navigation, while sophisticated routines and enhanced information retrieval tools elevate the overall user experience.

title: Developer bought 83 acres near Yosemite for $4m; US weighs land swap for road
content: A Nevada-based developer that bought 83 acres outside Yosemite for $4 million in 2024 is seeking a land exchange with the US government. The proposal could give the private property a direct road through a quarter-mile strip of Yosemite National Park. The same access plan was rejected in earlier legal battles, but the Trump administration is now considering it.

title: On his last day as Apple CEO, Tim Cook sends memo to employees
content: Tim Cook has sent his final memo to Apple employees on his last day as CEO, telling staff he is not leaving Apple but stepping away from a role he loved. John Ternus takes over as Apple CEO on September 1, while Cook becomes executive chairman. Read Tim Cook's full memo, his praise for Ternus, and what the handover means for Apple's hardware-first next chapter.

title: Economy grew 7.8% in Q1 despite Iran crisis and El Nino conditions
content: India's economy recorded impressive growth of 7.8% during the April to June quarter, driven by a thriving manufacturing sector and a strong services industry. Domestic demand surged, bolstered by significant increases in investment and exports. Reflecting this positive trend, the government has upgraded growth projections for prior financial years, showcasing the economy's robust resilience in the face of global challenges.

title: D4vd’s private lawyers withdraw from case: Why did he switch to a public defender?
content: D4vd’s private attorneys have withdrawn from representing him in the murder case involving 14-year-old Celeste Rivas Hernandez. During an August 31, 2026 hearing, the Los Angeles County Public Defender’s Office was appointed as his new legal team. Burke has pleaded not guilty, remains jailed without bail and faces multiple charges. After a July preliminary hearing found enough evidence for trial, his next court appearance is expected in October 2026.

title: Aaron Donald returns to Rams: Can he and Myles Garrett form the NFL’s best duo?
content: Aaron Donald’s comeback to the Los Angeles Rams for the 2026 season marks a thrilling return from retirement. Joining forces with the talented edge Myles Garrett, they form an intimidating pass rush that will test the mettle of any quarterback. With aspirations of clinching a Super Bowl title in their home stadium, this partnership heralds a fresh wave of defensive excellence for the Rams, reviving hopes for passionate fans.

title: Nepal floods: Avalanche raced down Himalayas at 167 kmph, triggering deadly deluge
content: A sudden ice-rock avalanche plummeted down the Himalayas, wreaking havoc in Nepal with catastrophic floods. This swift phenomenon covered extensive ground in mere moments, and scientists ruled out a glacial lake outburst flood as the cause. The disaster wreaked havoc on Nepal's hydropower facilities, prompting a call for further inquiries into the geological processes that led to this calamity.

title: IMD predicts below-normal rainfall over India in September
content: September rainfall across India is predicted to be below normal, concluding the monsoon season deficiently. August was the warmest on record, with several regions experiencing record high temperatures. Cumulative rainfall from June to August shows a significant deficit, impacting agricultural sowing and increasing irrigation costs. Strong El Niño conditions are expected to persist, negatively affecting monsoon rainfall patterns. Neutral Indian Ocean Dipole conditions will not benefit the monsoon this year.

title: India’s GPS problem: Why the armed forces need NavIC to work
content: India's NavIC satellite system, crucial for military and civilian use, currently has only three operational satellites. This shortfall impacts its ability to provide accurate positioning and navigation services. The system's reliability issues stemmed from imported atomic clocks, now being replaced by indigenous ones. Upcoming launches aim to restore the full constellation's functionality. This indigenous capability is vital for India's strategic autonomy and modernization efforts.

title: From exam reforms to school reforms: How CJP is changing political discourse
content: Student protests for improved school conditions have shifted from cities to villages across India.  The Cockroach Janata Party's campaign exposed poor government school infrastructure in several states.  State governments responded with new regulations and accelerated development projects.  Political parties are now focusing on youth outreach and educational issues.  This movement highlights youth as potential game-changers in electoral politics.

After an impressive career spanning nearly two decades, Messi guided his national team to triumph in the 2021 Copa America and the 2022 World Cup, as well as reaching the final of the 2026 World Cup. His departure signifies a deeply emotional farewell to a remarkable journey.

title: Why is it illegal to take sand from some beaches? Reasons you should know

Destinations like Sardinia and Hawaii impose stringent laws against the extraction of sand, pebbles, or shells, as these elements play a crucial role in combating coastal erosion and nurturing marine life. In India, rampant illegal sand mining devastates neighborhoods and ecosystems alike, exhausting this precious resource and igniting lasting repercussions.

content:

title: MBBS, BDS interns in J&K start indefinite strike over ‘low’ stipend
content:
File photo: MBBS interns of Government Medical College (GMC) Jammu and its associated hospital hold a poster during their protest demanding a hike in their monthly stipend.

JAMMU: MBBS and BDS interns across medical colleges in Jammu & Kashmir went on an indefinite strike on Monday, demanding an increase in their monthly stipend from Rs 12,300 to Rs 30,000. “Our stipend has remained stagnant for seven years, while in other states it ranges between Rs 25,000 and Rs 45,000 a month. We are performing the same duties, including 24-hour shifts and rural postings,” one of the protesters said. Protesters cited a health and medical education department committee which in 2023 recommended increasing the stipend to Rs 25,000 for the academic year 2025-26. Congress’ J&K unit chief Tariq Hameed Karra on Monday wrote to chief minister Omar Abdullah, urging a sympathetic and immediate consideration of the demand.

title: PM Modi's jackets, Rahul's shirts: How leaders use fashion for political messaging
content: a politician's clothes have helped construct identities, signal ideology, project modernity, invoke tradition and increasingly generate the kind of visual moments that social media loves . when Rahul Gandhi appeared in a pink shirt, the change from his usual white clothing drew attention online .

title: 'Golden age of America': Trump celebrates as SC clears $400M White House ballroom
content: Prisha Patnaik is a journalist with The Times of India, writing across geopolitics, international affairs, culture, history and internet culture. With over two years of experience in social media and digital content, she is interested in how news, politics and culture are shaped for digital audiences. She holds a master’s degree in Media and Communications from Goldsmiths, University of London.

title: Malicious ads on social media lure users into fraud: Centre
content: the national cybercrime threat analytics unit (NCTAU) warns of financial fraud via sideloaded malicious Android apps disguised as porn apps . misleading ads under the names Night Play, Reloop, Kyss, Riva, Vima, Nexo and Vixa redirect users to phishing websites featuring pornographic content . the app requests permissions that allow it to install additional applications, enabling fraudsters to take control of the device .

title: Alaska eliminates invasive pike and restocks lake with 6,836 Arctic char
content: biologists treated an entire lake with rotenone, a plant-derived piscicide, to wipe out an invasive population of northern pike . post-surveys confirmed the pike were gone . the next step was rebuilding what had been lost .
